name: Maze
metaTitle: Maze alternative for AI-built prototypes | Aero
description: Maze or Aero? Aero hosts a prototype from Claude, Figma or HTML, records your own testers, and gives transcripts on the free plan. What each does.
h1: A Maze alternative for AI-built prototypes
answer: Maze is a research platform with surveys, card sorting and a testing panel. Aero is narrower: it puts a prototype online at its own link, you send the link to your own testers, and you get a recording, transcript and summary of each session.
facts: Free plan includes recordings and transcripts
chooseThem: You need surveys, card sorting or tree testing as well as prototype tests.
You want a recruited panel of participants, not only people you invite.
Your team has an Enterprise budget and needs moderated interviews, mobile app testing or single sign-on.
chooseAero: Your prototype comes from Claude, ChatGPT, Lovable, Bolt or v0, or is a plain HTML file, as well as Figma.
You have a few people to send a link to and want a recording, transcript and summary back from each.
You want the free plan to include recordings and transcripts.
You want your prototype at its own address, with a password if you need one.

Read from Maze’s own pages on 21 Nov 2026. “Not stated” means the page didn’t say, not that Maze can’t do it. Plans and prices change, so check Maze’s pricing page.
faq: Is Aero a replacement for Maze?
Only for one job. Aero publishes a prototype and records your own testers. It has no panel, surveys, card sorting or tree testing, so teams that need those still need a tool like Maze.
Can I test a Claude or Lovable prototype in Maze?

Maze’s own pages describe Figma imports and live website testing for published sites. They don’t say whether a coded or AI-built prototype can be tested, so check with Maze. In Aero you publish it and test the link.
Do my testers need an account?
Not for Aero. They open your link, allow recording and start.
Does Aero find testers for me?
No. You send the link to your own people.
What does Aero cost?
Free has 3 test sessions with recordings and transcripts. Paid plans are $3, $6 and $19 a month, with a 7-day free trial.

name: UserTesting
metaTitle: UserTesting alternative for prototype tests | Aero
description: UserTesting finds participants for you. Aero hosts your prototype and records the people you invite, from $0 a month with transcripts on every plan.
h1: A UserTesting alternative for tests you run yourself
answer: UserTesting is an enterprise platform with its own network of participants. Aero is for the smaller job: you put a prototype online, send the link to people you already have, and get a recording, transcript and summary of each session.
chooseThem: You need participants found for you, with demographic filters and screener questions.
You need live conversations, a managed research programme or an enterprise contract.
You test with large groups across teams and countries.
chooseAero: You already have people to send a link to: colleagues, customers or a community.
You want to pay $0 to $19 a month, not per session or by quote.
Your prototype comes from Claude, ChatGPT, Lovable, Bolt, v0 or plain HTML as well as Figma.
rows: Free, then $3, $6 or $19 a month. No call

Read from UserTesting’s own pages on 21 Nov 2026. Its pages name the plans differently (Starter, Advanced, Ultimate on one; Advanced, Ultimate and Ultimate+ in its help centre), and its main pricing page didn’t load when we checked. “Not stated” means the page didn’t say, not that UserTesting can’t do it.
faq: Is Aero a UserTesting alternative?
For one job: testing a prototype with people you invite. Aero doesn’t find participants, run live conversations or sell enterprise plans.
Does Aero provide testers?
No. You send the test link to your own people, and they need no account.
What does UserTesting cost?
Its Starter plan is listed at $149 a session with a minimum purchase of 10 sessions. Higher plans are by quote. Check its plans page for current prices.
What do I get from each session in Aero?
The recording of the tester’s tab and voice, a transcript, and a summary with friction points. They arrive a minute or so after the session ends.
What does Aero cost?
Free has 3 test sessions with recordings and transcripts. Paid plans are $3, $6 and $19 a month, with a 7-day free trial.

h1: A Lyssna alternative for testing your own prototype
answer: Lyssna (formerly UsabilityHub) runs quick design tests and interviews, with a panel you can pay for. Aero does one thing: it hosts your prototype and records your own testers going through it, with a transcript and summary of each session.

You want recordings and transcripts on the free plan.
You want your prototype at its own address, with a password if you need one.

faq: Are Lyssna and UsabilityHub the same company?
Yes. UsabilityHub changed its name to Lyssna in October 2023, according to Lyssna’s own announcement.
Is Aero a replacement for Lyssna?
Only for one job. Aero publishes a prototype and records your own testers. It has no panel and no quick design studies.
Does Aero find testers for me?
No. You send the link to your own people, and they need no account.
Can I test a Lovable or Claude prototype in Aero?
Yes. Publish it to Aero, then start a test and pick that site. You get one link to send.
What does Aero cost?
Free has 3 test sessions with recordings and transcripts. Paid plans are $3, $6 and $19 a month, with a 7-day free trial.
